title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 118 (Minutes of proceedings of general meeting, meeting of Board of Directors and other meeting and resolutions passed by postal ballot)

content.overview: Section 118 requires prescribed minutes to be prepared, signed and maintained and gives duly recorded minutes evidentiary significance.
content.glance: Minutes of covered meetings and postal-ballot resolutions must be recorded in the prescribed manner within thirty days; applicable Secretarial Standards must be followed.
content.study:
## What must be recorded

Section 118 requires minutes of general meetings, meetings of classes of shareholders and creditors, Board meetings, and resolutions passed by postal ballot to be prepared, signed and kept in the relevant minute books in accordance with the Act and rules. The general statutory period for entering minutes is thirty days.

## Content and standards

Minutes should fairly record the proceedings and decisions. The Act restricts inclusion of matters that are defamatory, irrelevant or detrimental to the company's interests, subject to the statutory wording and the chairperson's role. Secretarial Standards approved and notified under section 118(10) are mandatory to the extent applicable; check the current notified standards, including SS-1 for Board meetings and SS-2 for general meetings.

## Evidentiary effect and integrity

Minutes duly kept under the section are evidence of the proceedings. The section also contains rules concerning inspection, preservation and penalties for tampering or default. Do not treat minutes as a substitute for compliance with notice, quorum or voting requirements.

## Practical checklist

Identify the meeting or resolution type; prepare the minutes promptly; record attendance, decisions and dissent as required by the applicable standards; obtain required signature; enter and preserve the record within the statutory period; and protect the integrity of the minute book.

sections.title: Preparation and maintenance
content: Record minutes for the meetings and postal-ballot resolutions covered by section 118.
The general statutory period is thirty days, subject to the section and applicable rules.

sections.title: Secretarial Standards
content: Comply with Secretarial Standards approved and notified under section 118(10) to the extent applicable.
Check the current standards for Board meetings and general meetings and the relevant company type.

sections.title: Evidentiary effect and integrity
content: Duly kept minutes are evidence of the proceedings, subject to the Act.
The section contains restrictions on content and rules protecting minute-book integrity; minutes do not cure defects in the meeting itself.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: A properly incorporated company was challenged as indistinct from its controlling shareholder.
cases.issue: What is the legal effect of incorporation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A registered company is a legal person separate from its members, even when control and ownership are concentrated.
cases.holding: The company's separate personality was affirmed.
cases.relevance: Use for Companies Act s. 9 and corporate personality.

cases.name: Foss v. Harbottle
cases.facts: Shareholders sought relief for alleged wrongs to the company.
cases.issue: Who may sue for a wrong done to the company and when may exceptions apply?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The company is the proper plaintiff for corporate wrongs, subject to recognised exceptions such as fraud on the minority and ultra vires acts.
cases.holding: The proper-plaintiff and majority-rule principles were established.
cases.relevance: Use with oppression, mismanagement and class-action analysis.

cases.name: Needle Industries (India) Ltd. v. Needle Industries Newey (India) Holding Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court examined share issue powers and alleged oppression.
cases.issue: When does a corporate action become oppressive or invalid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court examines purpose, fairness, statutory power and resulting prejudice rather than treating every irregularity as oppression.
cases.holding: The corporate action was assessed under the statutory and equitable framework.
cases.relevance: Use for share allotment and oppression claims.

cases.name: Miheer H. Mafatlal v. Mafatlal Industries Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court reviewed a scheme of arrangement sanctioned by the company court.
cases.issue: What is the court's role in sanctioning a corporate scheme?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The court must ensure statutory compliance, class fairness, informed approval and absence of illegality, but does not substitute its commercial judgment for the company's decision.
cases.holding: The principles governing scheme sanction were stated.
cases.relevance: Use for corporate arrangements and tribunal scrutiny.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the purpose and legal effect of minutes under section 118.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 118 requires minutes of specified company meetings and postal-ballot resolutions to be prepared, signed and kept in accordance with the Act and rules, generally within thirty days. Applicable notified Secretarial Standards must be followed. Duly kept minutes are evidence of proceedings, but do not independently cure defects in notice, quorum or voting.
